verses.pali: 20. Mahāvagga

verses.pali: Sotānugatasutta
verses.english: Followed by Ear

verses.pali: “Sotānugatānaṁ, bhikkhave, dhammānaṁ, vacasā paricitānaṁ, manasānupekkhitānaṁ, diṭṭhiyā suppaṭividdhānaṁ cattāro ānisaṁsā pāṭikaṅkhā.
verses.english: “Mendicants, you can expect four benefits when the teachings have been followed by ear, consolidated by voice, examined by the mind, and well comprehended theoretically.

verses.pali: Katame cattāro?
verses.english: What four?

verses.pali: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu dhammaṁ pariyāpuṇāti—
verses.english: Take a mendicant who memorizes the teaching—

verses.pali: suttaṁ, geyyaṁ, veyyākaraṇaṁ, gāthaṁ, udānaṁ, itivuttakaṁ, jātakaṁ, abbhutadhammaṁ, vedallaṁ.
verses.english: statements, mixed prose & verse, discussions, verses, inspired exclamations, legends, stories of past lives, amazing stories, and elaborations.

verses.pali: Tassa te dhammā sotānugatā honti, vacasā paricitā, manasānupekkhitā, diṭṭhiyā suppaṭividdhā.
verses.english: They’ve followed those teachings by ear, consolidated them by voice, examined them by the mind, and well comprehended them theoretically.

verses.pali: So muṭṭhassati kālaṁ kurumāno aññataraṁ devanikāyaṁ upapajjati.
verses.english: But they die unmindful and are reborn in one of the orders of gods.

verses.pali: Tassa tattha sukhino dhammapadā plavanti.
verses.english: Being happy there, passages of the teaching come back to them.

verses.pali: Dandho, bhikkhave, satuppādo;
verses.english: Memory comes up slowly,

verses.pali: atha so satto khippaṁyeva visesagāmī hoti.
verses.english: but then that being quickly reaches distinction.

verses.pali: Sotānugatānaṁ, bhikkhave, dhammānaṁ, vacasā paricitānaṁ, manasānupekkhitānaṁ, diṭṭhiyā suppaṭividdhānaṁ ayaṁ paṭhamo ānisaṁso pāṭikaṅkho.
verses.english: This is the first benefit you can expect when the teachings have been followed by ear, consolidated by voice, examined by the mind, and well comprehended theoretically.

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu dhammaṁ pariyāpuṇāti—
verses.english: Furthermore, take a mendicant who memorizes the teaching—

verses.pali: suttaṁ, geyyaṁ, veyyākaraṇaṁ, gāthaṁ, udānaṁ, itivuttakaṁ, jātakaṁ, abbhutadhammaṁ, vedallaṁ.
verses.english: statements, mixed prose & verse, discussions, verses, inspired exclamations, legends, stories of past lives, amazing stories, and elaborations.

verses.pali: Tassa te dhammā sotānugatā honti, vacasā paricitā, manasānupekkhitā, diṭṭhiyā suppaṭividdhā.
verses.english: They’ve followed those teachings by ear, consolidated them by voice, examined them by the mind, and well comprehended them theoretically.

verses.pali: So muṭṭhassati kālaṁ kurumāno aññataraṁ devanikāyaṁ upapajjati.
verses.english: But they die unmindful and are reborn in one of the orders of gods.

verses.pali: Tassa tattha na heva kho sukhino dhammapadā plavanti;
verses.english: Though they’re happy there, passages of the teaching don’t come back to them.

verses.pali: api ca kho bhikkhu iddhimā cetovasippatto devaparisāyaṁ dhammaṁ deseti.
verses.english: However, a mendicant with psychic powers, who has achieved mastery of the mind, teaches Dhamma to the assembly of gods.

verses.pali: Tassa evaṁ hoti:
verses.english: They think:

verses.pali: ‘ayaṁ vā so dhammavinayo, yatthāhaṁ pubbe brahmacariyaṁ acarin’ti.
verses.english: ‘I used to lead the spiritual life in this same teaching and training.’

verses.pali: Dandho, bhikkhave, satuppādo;
verses.english: Memory comes up slowly,

verses.pali: atha so satto khippameva visesagāmī hoti.
verses.english: but then that being quickly reaches distinction.

verses.pali: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, puriso kusalo bherisaddassa.
verses.english: Suppose a person was skilled in the sound of drums.

verses.pali: So addhānamaggappaṭipanno bherisaddaṁ suṇeyya.
verses.english: While traveling along a road they hear the sound of drums.

verses.pali: Tassa na heva kho assa kaṅkhā vā vimati vā:
verses.english: They wouldn’t have any doubts or uncertainties about whether

verses.pali: ‘bherisaddo nu kho, na nu kho bherisaddo’ti.
verses.english: that was the sound of drums or not.

verses.pali: Atha kho bherisaddotveva niṭṭhaṁ gaccheyya.
verses.english: They’d just conclude, ‘That’s the sound of drums.’

verses.pali: Evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu dhammaṁ pariyāpuṇāti—
verses.english: In the same way, take a mendicant who memorizes the teaching …

verses.pali: suttaṁ, geyyaṁ, veyyākaraṇaṁ, gāthaṁ, udānaṁ, itivuttakaṁ, jātakaṁ, abbhutadhammaṁ, vedallaṁ.
Tassa te dhammā sotānugatā honti, vacasā paricitā, manasānupekkhitā, diṭṭhiyā suppaṭividdhā.
So muṭṭhassati kālaṁ kurumāno aññataraṁ devanikāyaṁ upapajjati.
verses.english: But they die unmindful and are reborn in one of the orders of gods. …

Tassa evaṁ hoti:
‘ayaṁ vā so dhammavinayo, yatthāhaṁ pubbe brahmacariyaṁ acarin’ti.
Dandho, bhikkhave, satuppādo;

verses.english: but then that being quickly reaches distinction.

verses.english: This is the second benefit you can expect when the teachings have been followed by ear, consolidated by voice, examined by the mind, and well comprehended theoretically.

verses.english: But passages of the teaching don’t come back to them when they’re happy, nor does a mendicant with psychic powers … teach Dhamma to the assembly of gods.

verses.english: This is the third benefit you can expect when the teachings have been followed by ear, consolidated by voice, examined by the mind, and well comprehended theoretically.

verses.english: But they die unmindful and are reborn in one of the orders of gods.

verses.english: But passages of the teaching don’t come back to them when they’re happy, and neither a mendicant with psychic powers … nor a godling teaches Dhamma to the assembly of gods.

verses.pali: api ca kho opapātiko opapātikaṁ sāreti:
verses.english: But a being who has been reborn spontaneously reminds another such being:

verses.pali: ‘sarasi tvaṁ, mārisa, sarasi tvaṁ, mārisa, yattha mayaṁ pubbe brahmacariyaṁ acarimhā’ti.
verses.english: ‘Do you remember, good fellow? Do you remember where we used to lead the spiritual life?’

verses.pali: So evamāha:
verses.english: He says:

verses.pali: ‘sarāmi, mārisa, sarāmi, mārisā’ti.
verses.english: ‘I remember, good fellow, I remember!’

verses.pali: Dandho, bhikkhave, satuppādo;
verses.english: Memory comes up slowly,

verses.pali: atha so satto khippaṁyeva visesagāmī hoti.
verses.english: but then that being quickly reaches distinction.

verses.pali: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, dve sahāyakā sahapaṁsukīḷikā.
verses.english: Suppose there were two friends who had played together in the sand.

verses.pali: Te kadāci karahaci aññamaññaṁ samāgaccheyyuṁ.
verses.english: Some time or other they’d meet.

verses.pali: Añño pana sahāyako sahāyakaṁ evaṁ vadeyya:
verses.english: And one friend would say to the other:

verses.pali: ‘idampi, samma, sarasi, idampi, samma, sarasī’ti.
verses.english: ‘Do you remember this, dear? Do you remember that, dear?’

verses.pali: So evaṁ vadeyya:
verses.english: They’d say:

verses.pali: ‘sarāmi, samma, sarāmi, sammā’ti.
verses.english: ‘I remember, dear, I remember!’

verses.pali: Evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu dhammaṁ pariyāpuṇāti—
verses.english: In the same way, take a mendicant who memorizes the teaching …

verses.pali: suttaṁ, geyyaṁ, veyyākaraṇaṁ, gāthaṁ, udānaṁ, itivuttakaṁ, jātakaṁ, abbhutadhammaṁ, vedallaṁ.
Tassa te dhammā sotānugatā honti, vacasā paricitā, manasānupekkhitā, diṭṭhiyā suppaṭividdhā.
So muṭṭhassati kālaṁ kurumāno aññataraṁ devanikāyaṁ upapajjati.
verses.english: But they die unmindful and are reborn in one of the orders of gods. …

api ca kho opapātiko opapātikaṁ sāreti:
‘sarasi tvaṁ, mārisa, sarasi tvaṁ, mārisa, yattha mayaṁ pubbe brahmacariyaṁ acarimhā’ti.
So evamāha:
‘sarāmi, mārisa, sarāmi, mārisā’ti.
Dandho, bhikkhave, satuppādo;
verses.english: Memory comes up slowly,

verses.pali: atha kho so satto khippaṁyeva visesagāmī hoti.
verses.english: but then that being quickly reaches distinction.

verses.pali: Sotānugatānaṁ, bhikkhave, dhammānaṁ, vacasā paricitānaṁ, manasānupekkhitānaṁ, diṭṭhiyā suppaṭividdhānaṁ ayaṁ catuttho ānisaṁso pāṭikaṅkho.
verses.english: This is the fourth benefit you can expect when the teachings have been followed by ear, consolidated by voice, examined by the mind, and well comprehended theoretically.

verses.pali: Sotānugatānaṁ, bhikkhave, dhammānaṁ, vacasā paricitānaṁ, manasānupekkhitānaṁ diṭṭhiyā suppaṭividdhānaṁ ime cattāro ānisaṁsā pāṭikaṅkhā”ti.
verses.english: You can expect these four benefits when the teachings have been followed by ear, consolidated by voice, examined by the mind, and well comprehended theoretically.”

verses.pali: Paṭhamaṁ.
